title: SRE error-budget concordat and capacity play
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a single, actionable SRE "concordat" (a compact contract) between SRE and product/engineering owners that combines SLOs and error-budget governance with capacity planning, progressive throttles, incident review standards, and a template for reliability initiatives. The goal is consistent, predictable decision-making when service quality or capacity are under stress and to accelerate remediation with clear ownership.

Scope: applies to all customer-facing inference endpoints (hosted API, dedicated, private) and the platform services that materially affect those endpoints (router, kvcache, batching layer, model-serving pool).

Key principles
- Shared accountability: Product defines customer-impacting SLOs; SRE enforces runtime safety and operational levers when the error budget is exhausted.
- Graduated response: actions scale with error-budget consumption and forecasted capacity shortage, from advisory notices to automatic throttles and feature degradations.
- Fast feedback: incidents and reliability initiatives include short feedback loops with measurable success criteria.
- Observable and auditable: every action that affects routing/capacity must be recorded in the incident timeline and dashboard.

Definitions
- SLO: Service-level objective, example: "Model inference success rate >= 99.95% over 30 days".
- Error budget: 1 - SLO (e.g., 0.05% of requests/month).
- Burn rate: error-budget consumption rate vs. expected baseline (see formula below).
- Capacity hedge: reserved headroom (measured in GPU core-seconds or throughput RPS) maintained to absorb surges.

SLO math and example
- Measurement window: 30 days rolling by default for customer-facing endpoints.
- Example SLO: availability_slo = 99.95% (monthly).
- Monthly error budget fraction = 1 - 0.9995 = 0.0005 (0.05%).
- Burn rate (simplified): BurnRate = (ErrorsObserved / ErrorBudget) / (ElapsedWindowFraction)
  - If BurnRate > 4 sustained for 1 hour -> accelerated mitigation.

Error-budget governance matrix
- Advisory (<= 25% consumed over rolling window): notify owners; no automated action.
- Monitor (25% - 50%): SRE produces a short remediation plan; PM/Product owner notified; capacity forecast run.
- Intervention (50% - 80%): mandatory operational review within 2 business hours; prepare throttles/fallbacks and pre-authorize automated mitigations.
- Emergency (80% - 100%): enable progressive throttles and feature degradations; open incident channel; notify leadership.
- Exhausted (>100%): automatic hard throttles to preserve core SLOs; immediate postmortem required; reliability initiative proposal required.

Progressive throttling and graceful degradation runbook (operational steps)
1) Pre-checks (SRE responder)
   - Confirm SLO dashboard shows >80% error-budget consumed or burn rate trigger exceeded.
   - Confirm incident channel open and incident leader (IL) assigned.
   - Ensure feature-owners/PMs are paged.
2) Apply soft throttles (low-impact)
   - Toggle rate limit: set per-customer soft limit to 75% of baseline for non-SLA customers.
   - Command example (internal CLI):
     rcli throttle apply --scope non-sla --ratio 0.75 --reason "error-budget >80%"

3) Enable model-fallback policy
   - Route new requests to cost-stable/quantized model variant for non-critical routes.
   - Example routing config (YAML snippet):
     routeOverrides:
       - route: /v1/generate
         conditions:
           - customer_tier: "standard"
         action: fallback-model-quantized-v2

4) Activate burst pool and preemption policy
   - Scale up burst GPUs by terraform apply or cloud-scheduler: scale to N+20% reserve.
   - Command example: kubectl scale deployment/model-pool-burst --replicas=12

5) Hard throttle (if exhausted)
   - Reduce global RPS to preserve control-plane and core routes (e.g., tokenization / health checks remain).
   - Notify customers via status page and product comms.

Capacity planning and hedging cadence
- Monthly capacity forecast: each service owner provides 30/60/90-day forecast in the capacity ledger.
- Quarterly hedging review: SRE reviews current hedge vs. recent burst events; target hedge = max(10% of mean peak, 2h of sustained peak per region).
- Fast-path scaling: teams maintain an emergency bootstrap recipe (runbook) to add on-prem/GCP capacity and validation smoke tests.

Capacity hedging policy (summary table)
- Hedge type: Reserved (Dedicated pools) | Elastic (Burst GPU + spot) | Routing (degrade to lighter model)
- Target: Reserved = commit to 60% baseline; Elastic = provide 30% burst headroom; Routing = degrade 2 tiers automatically

Operational tooling and queries (examples)
- SLO dashboard: uses SLO-collector -> pre-aggregated windows; key panels: 30d SLO, 7d trend, burn-rate heatmap.
- PromQL sample (error rate):
  sum(rate(inference_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[5m]))
- Burn rate query (30d):
  (sum(inference_errors_window_30d) / (1 - ${SLO})) / (elapsed_fraction_30d)
- Incident evidence artifacts to collect automatically: request traces, model latency histogram, kvcache hit rate, GPU utilization, batch size distribution.

Incident review standard (post-incident template)
- Title and severity level.
- Timeline (ISO timestamps) with automated anchors for: alert -> mitigation -> resolution.
- Impact summary: customers affected, estimated RPS lost, revenue estimate if available.
- Root cause analysis: causal chain with evidence and hypothesis testing results.
- Detection & response analysis: how we detected it, time-to-detect, time-to-mitigate.
- What went well / what failed.
- Action items: concise tasks with owner (team/person), due date, and verification criteria.
- Link to artifact bundle: dashboards, logs, and the runbook steps executed.

Incident review success criteria (must be present for a published postmortem)
- Clear owner assigned for each action item.
- At least one action item is prioritized into a sprint or reliability initiative within 2 weeks.
- Verification plan and success metric defined (e.g., reduce similar-season burn rate by 60%).

Reliability initiative proposal template (how to convert actions into funded work)
1) Title and one-line summary.
2) Problem statement and impact (quantified).
3) Hypothesis and proposed change (configuration, code, capacity, tooling).
4) Success criteria (SLO delta, cost delta, ROI).
5) Implementation plan and roll-out strategy (canary, ramp, rollback).
6) Estimated effort (engineer-weeks) and cost delta.
7) Stakeholders and sign-off.

Escalation and communication matrix
- 1st responder: oncall SRE (PagerDuty P1) - immediate mitigation.
- SLO lead: Owner responsible for the SLO metric - short-term plan and prioritization.
- Product/PM: evaluate customer communications and feature prioritization.
- Engineering manager: approves capacity commits and budgeted hedges.
- Executive on-call: only for major incidents (impacting >10% customers or >$X/hr).

Auditability: every throttle/route change must create an audit event in the operational log and be included in the incident timeline. Example audit event schema (single-line JSON stored in infra logs):
{"event":"throttle_applied","actor":"sre:oncall","scope":"non-sla","ratio":"0.75","ticket":"INC-12345"}

Onboarding checklist for product teams (to avoid surprises)
- Agree on SLO and measurement windows during feature spec review.
- Nominate an SLO lead and provide a 90-day traffic forecast.
- Provide a degradation plan (what features can be throttled or degraded) and validate the rollback story in staging.

Runbook for SRE rotation handover (short)
1) Summary of current error-budget status and active mitigations.
2) Open tickets and active oncall tasks.
3) Known upcoming events: planned releases, marketing campaigns, or customer migrations.
4) Links to dashboards and last 24h alert runbook entries.

Appendix A — Example verification checklist for a reliability initiative
- Pre-merge: unit/integration tests + model regression evals.
- Canary: isolate 1% traffic for 6 hours, monitor SLO and utility metrics.
- Ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 30m minimum evaluation window between steps.
- Rollback criteria: >=2x baseline burn rate or >=1 critical user complaint per 100k requests.

Appendix B — Quick reference commands
- Toggle fallback: rcli config set routeOverrides --file /tmp/fallback.yaml
- Scale burst pool: kubectl scale deployment/model-pool-burst --replicas=12
- Create capacity ticket template: gissue create --project INF --title "Emergency GPU hedging" --assignee @infra-team --body "Forecasted shortage: X"

Owner and maintenance
- Document owner: SRE Reliability (Aisha Patel).
- Review cadence: this concordat is reviewed semi-annually or after any Severity-1 incident.
- Change process: edits require SRE+Product approval; page history must list reviewers and rationale.

Related pages and references

Feedback and improvements
- Use the page comments for minor feedback; major proposals should be submitted through the reliability initiative template and reviewed at the SRE quarterly reliability council.
